intro: To set up a workflow in Linear on Mac, open the team's settings from the sidebar, go to Automations, then rename, add or reorder the statuses your issues move through. Linear already creates a default workflow for each team, so you only change what does not match how your team works.
tldr: Each team in Linear gets a default workflow. You change it in Team settings, not inside a single issue.
On Mac, hover the team name in the sidebar, click the ··· menu, choose Team settings, then open Automations.
Statuses run in order. Rename, add or reorder them so the board matches the way your team really works.
Project statuses are a separate list. Team project statuses need a Business or Enterprise plan.

blocks.text: A workflow in Linear is the ordered list of statuses an issue moves through. Think of it as the lanes your work travels in, from the first idea to the finished job. Each team has its own workflow, so a design team and a support team can run different lanes in one workspace. This guide covers the Mac steps, the settings that matter, and the mistakes that cause trouble later.
What a workflow means in Linear

Linear's concept docs describe a workflow as a group of ordered issue statuses, defined per team. The word ordered matters. The order decides which status comes first, which comes next, and how columns line up when you open a board. If a status sits in the wrong place, people move issues in ways that make the board lie.

Linear also gives you a head start. It creates a default workflow for each team, and the docs say you can customize it in Team Settings. You rarely begin with a blank page. Open the default, keep what fits, rename what does not, and add a status only when you need one.
Check your plan and access first

Your plan sets how many teams you can have, and it decides which team-level features you get. Linear's pricing page lists the limits below. Check them before you design a big workflow, so you do not plan lanes for a team you cannot create.

items: Basic: $10 per user per month, billed yearly, with 5 teams and unlimited issues.
Business: $16 per user per month, billed yearly, with unlimited teams, private teams and guests.
Enterprise: custom pricing, billed annually only.

blocks.text: Access matters too. Linear's Teams doc says admins can restrict team creation to admin users under Settings, then Administration, then Security. If you can see Team settings but cannot change statuses, ask a workspace admin. I could not confirm a separate rule for who edits statuses, so ask rather than guess.
Step-by-step: open a team's workflow on Mac

The steps below follow the labels in the Linear desktop app. Labels can shift between releases, so read each one before you click. The path runs from the sidebar to Team settings, then to Automations, where the status list lives.
Add, rename and reorder statuses

Once you are in Automations, you do three jobs: rename, add and reorder. Rename first. A status called In progress means little to a support team that says Working on it. Use the words your team already uses in chat, so nobody has to translate them.

Add a status only when an issue really sits in that state for a while. Each extra status is one more thing people must update. Short lists are easier to keep honest. Reorder last. Once the names are set, the order is the flow, so check each move by asking whether an issue could skip backward.

blocks.text: Set up project statuses too

Issue statuses track one piece of work. Projects have their own status list, separate from the issue flow. The two lists look similar in the app, so keep them apart in your head before you edit either one.

Workspace admins edit project status names, descriptions and colors in Settings, then Projects, then Statuses. That list covers the whole workspace and works on every plan. Team project statuses sit under Team settings, then Team project statuses, and need Business or Enterprise. A September 24, 2026 changelog entry says teams can define their own project labels and statuses, and extend them to sub-teams.
Keyboard shortcuts for setup work
Linear has many shortcuts, but this page lists only the ones its own docs or changelogs confirm. Test any other shortcut in the app before you depend on it.

items: ⌘K opens the command bar. Type a view or action name and pick it from the list.
Esc clears the selected issues in a list or board view.
Shift with ↑ or ↓ extends a selection one issue at a time, after you select the first issue.
Comments send on Enter or on ⌘Enter. Choose the one you want in preferences.

blocks.text: Worked example: a five-status product workflow

Say you run a small product team. Work moves from an idea to a spec, then to build, review and release. The default statuses rarely match that, so you rename and add until they do. Start in Automations and rename the first status to Spec in progress.

Next, add Ready to build between the spec step and Building. Then drag Building and In review so they sit in that order. Shipped stays last. Keep the list at five. Two more statuses would add lanes that nobody uses.

Test the result with two test issues. Create them in the team, move one through each status, and watch where the card lands. If a card lands in the wrong column, the order is wrong. Delete the test issues when you finish, so the board starts clean.
Common mistakes when setting up a Linear workflow

items: Renaming statuses before the team agrees on the flow, so you rename everything twice.
Adding too many statuses. People then pick the nearest one, and the board stops telling the truth.
Reordering a status that already holds issues, then missing that some issues now sit in a lane that feels backward.
Looking for team project statuses on a Free or Basic plan, where they are not available.
Changing one team's statuses and expecting every team to follow. Each team has its own workflow.
Letting Enter send half-written comments. Switch the setting in preferences.

blocks.text: Most of these come from rushing the first pass. Agree on names and order with the people who move issues every day, then edit once. A short meeting saves three rounds of cleanup.
Check the workflow with time in status

Linear announced time in status on January 29, 2026. Hover over an issue's status indicator and you see the cumulative time it has spent in each status. You can also order by time in status, or filter with conditions such as In Review for more than 7 days.

That turns the workflow into a check. If issues sit in Building for weeks, the status may be too broad, or the work may be stuck. Read those numbers each week and adjust names or order when a lane tells you something is off.
Troubleshooting when changes do not stick

Most setup problems come from access, plan limits or an old app. Linear's March 12, 2026 UI refresh fixed a bug where workflow status saves could stay pending in Settings. If a save looks stuck, quit the desktop app, reopen it and check the status again.
Next steps after the workflow works

With the workflow set, the next job is getting work into it. Read [how to create an issue in Linear on Mac](/how-to/create-an-issue-in-linear) for shortcuts and templates, then build a view with [how to filter issues in Linear on Mac](/how-to/filter-issues-in-linear).

If your team plans in sprints, turn on cycles next. [How to create a cycle in Linear on Mac](/how-to/create-a-cycle-in-linear) walks through the team setting. Linear's desktop page lists a macOS download but no version number, so your labels may differ slightly from this page.

faq.question: Does Linear create a workflow for my team automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. Linear creates a default workflow for each team, and its concept docs say you can customize it in Team Settings. You only need to change what does not match how your team works.

faq.question: Where do I edit statuses on Mac?
faq.answer: Hover over the team name in the sidebar, click the ··· menu, choose Team settings, then open Automations. Statuses are edited in that section. If your version labels things differently, look for the team's Automations area.

faq.question: Can two teams have different workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. A workflow is defined per team. Set each team's statuses separately, because a change to one team's list does not reshape another team's board.

faq.question: Do I need a paid plan to change the workflow?
faq.answer: The docs I checked do not say basic workflow editing needs a paid plan. Team project statuses and private teams do need Business or Enterprise. Free allows 2 teams, Basic allows 5, and Business allows unlimited teams.

faq.question: What is the difference between issue statuses and project statuses?
faq.answer: Issue statuses track one piece of work. Project statuses track a project. Workspace project statuses live in Settings, then Projects, then Statuses. Team project statuses sit in Team settings and need Business or Enterprise.

faq.question: Is there a shortcut to open Team settings?
faq.answer: Press ⌘K to open the command bar, then type Team settings if it appears in the results. I could not confirm a dedicated Settings shortcut in Linear's docs, so use the sidebar path if the command bar does not list it.

faq.question: How do I see how long an issue stayed in a status?
faq.answer: Hover over the status indicator on the issue. Linear's time in status feature, announced January 29, 2026, shows the cumulative time spent in each status.

faq.question: Why does my screen look different from these steps?
faq.answer: Linear updates its desktop app often, and I could not confirm the current Mac version from an official page. Menu labels and layout may change, so read the label on your screen and match its meaning to the step.

task: Set up a team workflow in Linear on Mac
appliesTo: Linear desktop app on macOS, team workflows and project statuses
requirements: A Mac with the Linear desktop app, or Linear in a browser
Access to the team you want to change
A workspace admin if Team settings is missing for you
Business or Enterprise plan only if you need team project statuses
A short list of status names your team already uses

steps.name: Open the Linear desktop app
steps.text: Open Linear on your Mac and sign in to the workspace that holds the team. If you do not have the app yet, Linear's desktop page links a macOS download. The same steps work in a browser, but labels may differ slightly.
steps.tip: Make sure you are in the workspace that owns the team, or you will edit the wrong list.

steps.name: Find the team in the sidebar
steps.text: Look under Your teams in the sidebar and find the team whose workflow you want to change. Hover your pointer over the team name so the row shows its extra controls.
steps.tip: Each team has its own workflow, so change only the team you mean.

steps.name: Open the ··· menu
steps.text: With the team name hovered, click the ··· button on that row. The menu opens with the team actions.
steps.tip: If the button does not show, move the pointer off the row and back on.

steps.name: Choose Team settings
steps.text: Select Team settings from the menu. The settings page for that team opens. If you prefer the keyboard, press ⌘K and type Team settings, then choose it from the results if it appears.
steps.tip: The command bar shows the actions it finds, so the list may differ from this page.

steps.name: Open Automations
steps.text: In Team settings, open Automations. Linear's Teams doc says this section covers customizing workflows, adding and editing statuses, git automations, and auto-close and auto-archive.
steps.tip: Git automations and auto-close sit in the same section, so avoid changing them by accident while you edit statuses.

steps.name: Rename the statuses
steps.text: Select the status you want to change and edit its name. Use the names your team already says in chat, so nobody has to translate them. Rename only what you need, and keep the default for anything that already fits.
steps.tip: Controls can look slightly different between releases, so read the labels on your screen before you type.

steps.name: Add or remove a status
steps.text: Use the add control in the status list to create a status for a state that lasts long enough to track. Give it a name and check which category it belongs to before you save. Leave out any status an issue would never sit in for long.
steps.tip: Search excerpts of Linear's docs suggest each category keeps at least one status. If a delete fails, add another status in that category first.

steps.name: Reorder the flow
steps.text: Drag statuses into the order your work really moves. Read the list from top to bottom and ask whether an issue could skip a step. Fix any step that feels backward before you move on.
steps.tip: Reordering changes the column order on the board, so check the board after you save.

steps.name: Set project statuses if you need them
steps.text: For workspace project statuses, go to Settings, then Projects, then Statuses. Admins edit names, descriptions and colors there, and this works on every plan. Team project statuses sit in Team settings and need Business or Enterprise.
steps.tip: Check your plan before you hunt for the team option, because it is not available on Free or Basic.

steps.name: Check the result on the board
steps.text: Open the team's issues and switch to the board view. Look at the columns and their order. Move one test issue through each status, then delete the test issue when you finish.
steps.tip: Test with one issue at a time, so a shared board does not fill up with leftovers.

troubleshooting.problem: Team settings is missing from the ··· menu
troubleshooting.fix: Make sure you clicked the ··· on the team row, not a project row. If it still does not show, ask a workspace admin to confirm your access. Admins can also limit team creation under Settings, then Administration, then Security.

troubleshooting.problem: A status change does not save or stays pending
troubleshooting.fix: Linear's March 12, 2026 UI refresh fixed workflow saves that could get stuck in a pending state. Quit the desktop app, reopen it, and check the status again. If the problem continues, report it to Linear with the team name, the status name and what you clicked.
Search excerpts of Linear's docs say each category keeps at least one status. Add a new status in the same category first, then remove the old one and try again.
Team project statuses need a Business or Enterprise plan. On Free or Basic you only see workspace project statuses. Compare plans on Linear's pricing page before you upgrade.

troubleshooting.problem: Enter sends a comment before you finish
troubleshooting.fix: Open your account preferences in Linear and choose the setting that sends comments on Cmd Enter. The option lives on Linear's web settings page for account preferences.
Free allows 2 teams and Basic allows 5. Business and Enterprise are unlimited. Change your plan, or remove a team you no longer need if your plan lets you.
